title.zh: 卷一百九十六 列傳第八十三: 忠義四
title.en: Volume 196 Biographies 83: Loyal and Righteous Acts 4
title.raw: 卷一百九十六 列傳第八十三: 忠義四 Volume 196 Biographies 83: Loyal and Righteous Acts 4

sentences.zh: 普顏不花，字希古，蒙古氏。

translations.literal: Puyan Buhua, courtesy name Xigu, was of the Mongol clan.
translations.idiomatic: Puyan Buhua, whose courtesy name was Xigu, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 倜儻有大志。

translations.literal: He was unconventional and possessed great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 至正五年，由國子生登右榜進士第一人，授翰林修撰，調河南行省員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhizheng, as a student of the Imperial Academy he placed first on the right examination roster for the jinshi degree, was appointed Hanlin Academician Compiler, and was transferred to be Assistant Department Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1345, as an Imperial Academy student he topped the right roster of jinshi graduates, was made Hanlin Academician Compiler, and was posted as Assistant Department Director on the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷江西行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be Director of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 he was moved to Director of the Left and Right Bureaus on the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蘄黃徐壽輝來寇，普顏不花戰守之功為多，語在《道童傳》。

translations.literal: When Xu Shouhui of Qihuang came to raid, Puyan Buhua's merits in fighting and defending were the greatest; the account is in the biography of Daotong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shouhui of Qihuang invaded, Puyan Buhua accounted for most of the fighting and defense; that story is told in the biography of Daotong.

sentences.zh: 十六年，除江西廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356 he was made Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召還，授益都路達魯花赤，遷山東廉訪使，再轉為中書參知政事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was recalled and appointed Darughachi of Yidu Circuit, then promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong, and again transferred to be Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was recalled, named Darughachi of Yidu Circuit, promoted to Shandong Surveillance Commissioner, and later made Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔與治書侍御史李國鳳同經略江南。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered together with Investigating Censor Li Guofeng to oversee military affairs in the south.
translations.idiomatic: In 1358 an edict sent him with Investigating Censor Li Guofeng to direct operations in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 至建寧，江西陳友諒遣鄧克明來寇，而平章政事阿魯溫沙等皆夜遁。

translations.literal: When he reached Jianning, Chen Youliang of Jiangxi sent Deng Keming to attack, while the Grand Councilors Aruwinsha and others all fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianning, Chen Youliang of Jiangxi sent Deng Keming against the city, while Grand Councilors such as Aruwinsha fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 國鳳時分鎮延平，城陷，遁去。

translations.literal: Guofeng was then stationed separately at Yanping; the city fell and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guofeng was holding Yanping separately; when that city fell he escaped.

sentences.zh: 普顏不花曰：「我承制來此，去將何之？

translations.literal: Puyan Buhua said: "I came here by imperial commission—where would I go if I left?
translations.idiomatic: Puyan Buhua said, "I was sent here on imperial orders. If I leave, where shall I go?

sentences.zh: 誓與此城同存亡耳。

translations.literal: I swear to live or die with this city.
translations.idiomatic: I swear to stand or fall with this city."

sentences.zh: 」命築各門甕城，前後拒戰六十四日，既而大敗賊眾。

translations.literal: " He ordered barbicans built at every gate; for sixty-four days they fought off attacks before and after, and in the end routed the rebel host greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He had barbicans raised at each gate and held the enemy off for sixty-four days before routing them in a major victory.

sentences.zh: 明年，召還，授山東宣慰使，再轉知樞密院事、平章山東行省，守禦益都。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled and appointed Pacification Commissioner of Shandong, then again transferred to be Vice Director of the Privy Council and Grand Councilor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, defending Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled, made Shandong Pacification Commissioner, then Vice Director of the Privy Council and Grand Councilor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, charged with defending Yidu.

sentences.zh: 大明兵壓境，普顏不花捍城力戰。

translations.literal: When the Great Ming army pressed the border, Puyan Buhua defended the city and fought with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: As Ming forces pressed the frontier, Puyan Buhua threw himself into the defense.

sentences.zh: 城陷，而平章政事保保出降。

translations.literal: The city fell, and the Grand Councilor Baobao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Grand Councilor Baobao went over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 普顏不花還告其母曰：「兒忠孝不能兩全，有二弟，當為終養。

translations.literal: Puyan Buhua returned and told his mother: "A son cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety at once; I have two younger brothers who should provide for you in your old age.
translations.idiomatic: Puyan Buhua went home and told his mother, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be kept—I have two younger brothers who must see to your final years.

sentences.zh: 」拜母，趨官舍，坐堂上。

translations.literal: " He bowed to his mother, hurried to the government compound, and sat in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed to her, went straight to the yamen, and took his seat in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 主將素聞其賢，召之再三，不往。

translations.literal: The commander had long heard of his worth and summoned him again and again, but he would not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming commander, who had long admired him, summoned him repeatedly, but he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 既而面縛之，普顏不花曰：「我元朝進士，官至極品，臣各為其主。

translations.literal: Presently they bound him facing forward; Puyan Buhua said: "I am a jinshi graduate of the Yuan dynasty, risen to the highest rank; each minister serves his own lord.
translations.idiomatic: They soon bound him before their ranks. Puyan Buhua said, "I was a Yuan jinshi who rose to the highest offices; every subject serves his own sovereign.

sentences.zh: 」不屈，死之。

translations.literal: " He would not submit and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not yield and was executed.

sentences.zh: 先是，其妻阿魯真，歷呼家人告之曰：「我夫受國恩，我亦封齊國夫人，今事至此，唯有死耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, his wife Aruzhen had called out to the household one by one and told them: "My husband has received the state's grace, and I too have been enfeoffed Lady of Qi; now that matters have come to this, there is nothing but death.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, his wife Aruzhen had gathered the household and said, "My husband owes the dynasty his life, and I was enfeoffed Lady of Qi; now there is nothing left but to die.

sentences.zh: 」家人莫不嘆息泣下。

translations.literal: " The family could only sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone wept and lamented.

sentences.zh: 已而普顏不花二弟之妻，各抱幼子，及婢妾，溺舍南井死。

translations.literal: Before long the wives of Puyan Buhua's two younger brothers, each holding an infant son, together with maids and concubines, drowned themselves in the south well of the residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the wives of his two younger brothers, each clutching a small son, with maids and concubines, drowned themselves in the south well.

sentences.zh: 比阿魯真欲下，而井填咽不可容，遂抱子投舍北井。

translations.literal: When Aruzhen was about to go down as well, the well was choked full and would not hold her; she then embraced her child and threw herself into the north well of the residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Aruzhen tried to follow, the well was already blocked and would not take her; she embraced her child and leapt into the north well instead.

sentences.zh: 其女及妾女、孫女，皆隨溺焉。

translations.literal: Her daughter, the daughters of concubines, and granddaughters all drowned with her.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter, the concubines' daughters, and granddaughters drowned with them.

sentences.zh: 是時有申榮者，平章山東行省，守東昌，榮見列郡皆降，告其父曰：「人生世間，不能全忠孝者，兒也。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Shen Rong, Grand Councilor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, defending Dongchang; Rong saw that every neighboring commandery had surrendered and told his father: "In this world, one who cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial piety in full is his son.
translations.idiomatic: About then Shen Rong, Grand Councilor of the Shandong Branch Secretariat, was holding Dongchang. Seeing every district surrender, he told his father, "In this life, the son who cannot keep both loyalty and filial piety whole is me.

sentences.zh: 」父曰：「何為？

translations.literal: " His father said: "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: " His father asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「城中兵少不敵，戰則萬人之命由兒而廢，但有一死報國耳。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "The troops in the city are too few to match the enemy; if we fight, the lives of ten thousand men will be ruined by me—there is only dying to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said, "We have too few men to stand against them; if I fight, I destroy ten thousand lives—only one death repays the state.

sentences.zh: 」遂自經。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 閔本，字宗先，河內人。

translations.literal: Min Ben, courtesy name Zongxian, was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Min Ben, whose courtesy name was Zongxian, came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 性剛正敏給，而刻志於學。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, sharp, and quick, and he set his will firmly on learning.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, sharp, and quick by nature, he devoted himself single-mindedly to study.

sentences.zh: 早歲得推擇為禮部令史，御史大夫不花奇本之才，辟以為掾，平反冤獄，甚有聲。

translations.literal: In his early years he was selected as a clerical officer of the Ministry of Rites; the Censor-in-Chief Buhua regarded his talent as extraordinary and recruited him as a staff member; he reversed wrongful convictions and gained great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he was chosen as a Ministry of Rites clerk; Censor-in-Chief Buhua prized his talent and took him on staff, where he overturned wrongful convictions and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 擢御史臺照磨。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Registrar of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Registrar of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷樞密院都事，拜監察御史，遷中書左司都事，五轉為吏部尚書，移刑、戶二部，皆以能見稱。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to be Director of the Privy Council, appointed Investigating Censor, moved to be Director of the Left Bureau of the Central Secretariat, and after five transfers became Minister of Personnel, then shifted to the Ministries of Punishments and Revenue—all were known for his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Privy Council Director, then Investigating Censor, then Director of the Central Secretariat's Left Bureau; after five moves he became Minister of Personnel and later headed Punishments and Revenue, earning renown for ability at each post.

sentences.zh: 本素貧，且有目疾，嘗上章乞謝事，不允，詔授集賢侍講學士。

translations.literal: Ben had always been poor and also suffered from eye disease; he once submitted a memorial requesting to resign, but it was not granted; he was ordered to be appointed Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Ben had long been poor and afflicted with eye trouble; he once asked to retire but was refused and instead made Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 大明兵薄京師，本謂其妻程氏曰：「國事至此，吾知之久矣。

translations.literal: When the Great Ming army pressed close to the capital, Ben told his wife Lady Cheng: "The state has come to this—I have known it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: As Ming troops closed on the capital, Ben told his wife Lady Cheng, "The dynasty has come to this—I have seen it coming for a long time.

sentences.zh: 愧不能立功補報，敢愛六尺軀苟活哉！

translations.literal: I am ashamed that I could not establish merit to repay it—how dare I cherish this six-foot frame and live on in disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed I could do nothing to repay it—how can I cling to this body and live on in shame?

sentences.zh: 」程氏曰：「君能死忠，我尚有愛於君乎！

translations.literal: " Lady Cheng said: "If you can die in loyalty, do I still have any attachment to you!
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Cheng said, "If you will die for the dynasty, what hold do I still have on you?

sentences.zh: 」本乃朝服，與程氏北向再拜，大​​書於屋壁曰：「元中奉大夫、集賢侍講學士閔本死。

translations.literal: " Ben then put on court dress and, together with Lady Cheng, bowed twice facing north, and wrote large characters on the wall of the house: "Min Ben, Recipient of Grace of the Middle Rank, Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, dies.
translations.idiomatic: " Ben donned court dress; he and Lady Cheng bowed twice to the north and he wrote large characters on the wall: "Min Ben, Recipient of Grace of the Middle Rank, Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, dies here.

sentences.zh: 」遂各縊焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon each hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 二女：長真真，次女女，見本死，呼天號泣，亦自縊於其傍。

translations.literal: His two daughters—the elder Zhenzhen and the younger Nü—seeing Ben dead, cried to heaven and wept, and also hanged themselves beside him.
translations.idiomatic: His daughters Zhenzhen and Nü, seeing him dead, wailed to heaven and hanged themselves at his side.

sentences.zh: 有拜住者，康里人也，字聞善。

translations.literal: There was one Baizhu, a man of the Kangli people, courtesy name Wenshan.
translations.idiomatic: There was Baizhu of the Kangli people, whose courtesy name was Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 以材累官至翰林國史院都事，為太子司經。

translations.literal: Through his talent he rose step by step to be Director of the Hanlin National History Academy, and served as Tutor in the Classics for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Talent carried him step by step to Director of the Hanlin National History Academy and Tutor in the Classics for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兵至，拜住謂家人曰：「吾始祖海藍伯封河東公者，與太祖同事王可汗，太祖取王可汗，收諸部落，吾祖引數十騎馳西北方，太祖使人追問之，曰：'昔者與皇帝同事王可汗，王可汗今已滅，欲為之報仇，則帝乃天命；

translations.literal: When the army arrived, Baizhu told his household: "My founding ancestor Hailanbo, enfeoffed Duke of Hedong, together with the Taizu served Prince Wang Khan; when the Taizu took Wang Khan and gathered the tribes, my ancestor led several dozen horsemen and galloped to the northwest. The Taizu sent men to pursue and question him; he said: 'In former days I served the Emperor together with Wang Khan; Wang Khan is now destroyed—if I wished to avenge him, the Emperor is Heaven's mandate; if I wished to change and serve the Emperor, my heart could not bear it—therefore I withdrew to a distant place to end my life.'
translations.idiomatic: When the armies came, Baizhu told his family, "Our forebear Hailanbo, enfeoffed Duke of Hedong, had served Prince Wang Khan alongside the Founder; when the Founder overthrew Wang Khan and gathered the tribes, our ancestor rode off northwest with a few dozen men. The Founder sent pursuers to ask why; he answered, 'I once served the Prince with the Emperor; the Prince is gone—if I avenged him I would fight Heaven's chosen; if I turned to serve the Emperor my heart could not bear it—so I withdrew to a distant land to end my days.'

sentences.zh: 欲改事帝，則吾心有所不忍，故避之於遠地，以沒吾生耳。

translations.literal: This is what my ancestor said.
translations.idiomatic: That was my ancestor's word.

sentences.zh: '此吾祖之言也。

translations.literal: And my ancestor was born in the northern desert—his words were still such; now I was born and raised in the Central Plains, reading books in the state academy—how could I not know great righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Born on the northern steppe, he still spoke so; I was raised in the Central Plains and schooled at the Imperial Academy—how could I not know what righteousness demands?

sentences.zh: 且吾祖生朔漠，其言尚如此，今吾生長中原，讀書國學，而可不知大義乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, my forebears received the state's thick grace, and I too have eaten its salary; now that its state is broken, how could I still bear to look upon it!
translations.idiomatic: My forebears received the dynasty's deep favor, and I have lived on its stipend; now the state is broken—how can I still face the world!

sentences.zh: 況吾上世受國厚恩，至吾又食祿，今其國破，尚忍見之！

translations.literal: Rather than live on in disgrace, it is better to die.
translations.idiomatic: Better to die than linger on in shame.

sentences.zh: 與其苟生，不如死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went and drowned himself in a well.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 」遂赴井死。

translations.literal: His household buried him east of the residence and burned all his books as funerary objects.
translations.idiomatic: His family buried him east of the house and burned all his books to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 其家人瘞之舍東，悉以其書籍焚之為殉云。

translations.literal: Zhao Hongyi, courtesy name Renqing, was a man of Jin Prefecture in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hongyi, whose courtesy name was Renqing, came from Jin Prefecture in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 趙弘毅，字仁卿，真定晉州人。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; his family was poor and had no books, so he hired himself out to a great household—by day he worked as a servant, by night he borrowed books to read.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning; too poor to own books, he hired himself to a wealthy house, laboring by day and reading borrowed books by night.

sentences.zh: 少好學，家貧無書，傭於巨室，晝則為役，夜則藉書讀之。

translations.literal: Some who pitied his resolve only had him oversee the work without making him labor.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his resolve, his employer sometimes let him supervise the work instead of toiling himself.

sentences.zh: 或閔其志，但使總其事而不役焉。

translations.literal: He once received instruction in the classics from Wu Cheng of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics under Wu Cheng of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗受經於臨川吳澄。

translations.literal: He once received instruction in the classics from Wu Cheng of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics under Wu Cheng of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 始辟翰林書寫，再轉為國史院編修官，調大樂署令。

translations.literal: He was first recruited as a Hanlin copyist, then again transferred to be Compiler of the National History Academy, and appointed Director of the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Hanlin copyist, became National History Compiler, and was appointed Director of the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 大明兵入京城，弘毅嘆息曰；

translations.literal: When the Great Ming army entered the capital, Hongyi sighed and said:
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces entered the capital, Hongyi sighed and said,

sentences.zh: 「忠臣不二君，烈女不二夫，此古語也。

translations.literal: "A loyal minister does not serve two lords, a chaste woman does not follow two husbands—this is the ancient saying.
translations.idiomatic: "A loyal minister does not serve two masters, a steadfast woman does not follow two husbands—that is the old saying.

sentences.zh: 我今力不能救社稷，但有一死報國耳。

translations.literal: Today I lack the strength to save the altars of state—there is only one death to repay the country.
translations.idiomatic: I lack the strength to save the realm—only death can repay it.

sentences.zh: 」乃與妻解氏皆自縊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and his wife Lady Xie both hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " He and his wife Lady Xie hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 其子恭，中書管勾，與妻子訣曰：「今乘輿北奔，我父子食祿，不能效尺寸力，吾父母已死，尚何敢愛死乎！

translations.literal: His son Gong, a Secretariat clerk, took leave of his wife and children, saying: "Now the imperial carriage flees north—we father and son have eaten the state's salary yet cannot exert even a little strength; my parents are already dead—how dare I still cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong, a Secretariat clerk, bade his wife and children farewell: "The Son of Heaven flees north; we have eaten the state's grain yet cannot lift a finger; my parents are dead—how dare I spare my life?

sentences.zh: 」或止之曰：「我曹官卑，何自苦如此。

translations.literal: Some tried to stop him, saying: "We officials are low in rank—why torment ourselves so?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him, "We are only minor officials—why suffer so?

sentences.zh: 」恭叱曰：「爾非我徒也。

translations.literal: " Gong rebuked them: "You are not my kind!
translations.idiomatic: " Gong snapped, "You are not my sort!

sentences.zh: 古者，忠義人各儘自心，豈問職之崇卑乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity, each man of loyalty and righteousness fulfilled his own heart—how would he ask whether his office was lofty or low!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity loyal men followed their own hearts—who asked whether rank was high or low?

sentences.zh: 」遂公服北向再拜，亦縊死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he put on official dress, bowed twice facing north, and also hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He donned official robes, bowed twice to the north, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 恭女官奴，年十七，見恭死，方大泣，適鄰嫗數輩來，相率出避，曰：「我未適人，避將何之？

translations.literal: Gong's daughter Guannu, seventeen years old, seeing Gong dead, was wailing loudly when several neighboring women came and urged her out to flee together.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's daughter Guannu, seventeen, was wailing over his body when neighboring women came to flee with her.

sentences.zh: 」不聽，嫗欲力挽之，女曰：「人生在世，便百歲亦須一死。

translations.literal: They would not listen; the women tried to pull her by force; the girl said: "In human life, even at a hundred years one must still die once.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed her; she said, "In this life, even at a hundred one must die once.

sentences.zh: 」乃潛入中堂，解衣帶自經。

translations.literal: " She then slipped into the central hall, untied her belt, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She slipped into the central hall and hanged herself with her belt.

sentences.zh: 鄭玉，字子美，徽州歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yu, courtesy name Zimei, was a man of She County in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yu, whose courtesy name was Zimei, came from She County in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟嗜學，既長，覃思《六經》，尤邃於《春秋》，絕意仕進，而勤於教。

translations.literal: As a child he was keen and fond of learning; when grown he pondered deeply the Six Classics, especially mastering the Spring and Autumn Annals; he utterly renounced seeking office and devoted himself to teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and studious as a boy, he later immersed himself in the Six Classics, especially the Spring and Autumn Annals, renounced office entirely, and threw himself into teaching.

sentences.zh: 學者門人受業者眾，所居至不能容。

translations.literal: Students and disciples who received his instruction were many; his dwelling could no longer hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils and disciples flocked to him until his house could hold no more.

sentences.zh: 學者相與即其地構師山書院以處焉。

translations.literal: The scholars together chose that place to build the Shishan Academy to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars built the Shishan Academy on that site to house them all.

sentences.zh: 玉為文章，不事雕刻煅煉，流傳京師，揭徯斯、歐陽玄咸加稱賞。

translations.literal: In Yu's essays he did not pursue carving and refining; when they circulated in the capital, Jie Xisi and Ouyang Xuan all praised them highly.
translations.idiomatic: His essays avoided ornament; when they reached the capital, Jie Xisi and Ouyang Xuan praised them warmly.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，朝廷除玉翰林待制、奉議大夫，遣使者賜以御酒名幣，浮海征之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng the court appointed Yu Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and Recipient of Grace, Grand Master of Discussion, and sent envoys bearing imperial wine and famous silks, crossing the sea to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 the court named him Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and Recipient of Grace, Grand Master of Discussion, and sent envoys with imperial wine and fine silks across the sea to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 玉辭疾不起，而為表以進曰：「名爵者，祖宗之所以遺陛下，​​使與天下賢者共之者，陛下不得私予人。

translations.literal: Yu declined on grounds of illness and did not rise, but submitted a memorial saying: "Titles and salaries are what the ancestors bequeathed to Your Majesty to share with the worthy of the world—the Majesty may not bestow them privately.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pleaded illness and stayed home, submitting a memorial: "Rank and stipend are what your forebears left you to share with the empire's worthies—Your Majesty may not grant them privately.

sentences.zh: 待制之職，臣非其才，不敢受。

translations.literal: The post of Attendant-in-Waiting—I am not fit for its duties and dare not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: I am unfit for Attendant-in-Waiting and dare not accept it.

sentences.zh: 酒與幣，天下所以奉陛下，陛下得以私與人，酒與幣，臣不敢辭也。

translations.literal: Wine and silks are what the world offers to Your Majesty, which Your Majesty may give privately to others; as for wine and silks, I dare not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Wine and silks are what the realm offers Your Majesty, which you may give privately—I dare not refuse those.

sentences.zh: 」玉既不仕，則家居，日以著書為事，所著有《周易纂注》。

translations.literal: " Since Yu would not serve, he remained at home, passing each day in writing books; among his works is Collected Commentary on the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: " Unwilling to serve, he stayed home writing; among his works is Collected Commentary on the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大明兵入徽州，守將將要致之，玉曰：「吾豈事二姓者耶！

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the Great Ming army entered Huizhou, the defending commander was about to bring him in; Yu said: "How could I serve two surnames!
translations.idiomatic: In 1357, when Ming troops entered Huizhou, the garrison commander meant to present him; Yu said, "How could I serve two dynasties?"

sentences.zh: 」因被拘囚。

translations.literal: " He was therefore imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " He was detained.

sentences.zh: 久之，親戚朋友攜具餉之，則從容為之盡歡，且告以必死狀。

translations.literal: After a long while, relatives and friends brought food to feed him; he then at ease made merry with them and told them he would certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while kinsmen brought food; he feasted with them calmly and told them he would die.

sentences.zh: 其妻聞之，使語之曰：「君苟死，吾其相從地下矣。

translations.literal: His wife hearing this sent word: "If you are resolved to die, I shall follow you underground.
translations.idiomatic: His wife sent word, "If you die, I will follow you to the grave."

sentences.zh: 」玉使謂之曰：「若果從吾死，吾其無憾矣。

translations.literal: Yu sent reply: "If you truly follow me in death, I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "If you truly follow me, I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」明日，具衣冠，北向再拜，自縊而死。

translations.literal: " The next day he put on cap and robes, bowed twice facing north, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he dressed in full regalia, bowed twice to the north, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 黃冔，字殷士，撫州金溪人。

translations.literal: Huang Yi, courtesy name Yinshi, was a man of Jinxi in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi, whose courtesy name was Yinshi, came from Jinxi in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 博學明經，善屬文，尤長於詩。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, clear in the classics, skilled in composition, especially accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Learned in the classics, skilled at prose, and especially gifted in poetry.

sentences.zh: 至正十七年，用左丞相太平奏，授淮南行省照磨，未行，除國子助教，遷太常博士，轉國子博士，升監丞，擢翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhizheng, on the memorial of Left Chancellor Taiping, he was appointed Registrar of the Huainan Branch Secretariat; before he set out he was made Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education, transferred to Doctor of the Grand Sacrificial Office, then Doctor of the Directorate, promoted to Vice Director, and elevated to Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting, concurrently Compiler of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1357, on Left Chancellor Taiping's recommendation, he was named Huainan Branch Registrar; before departing he became Directorate Assistant Instructor, Grand Sacrificial Office Doctor, then Directorate Doctor, Vice Director, and Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting with a concurrent National History compile.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，京城既破，冔歎曰：「我以儒致身，累蒙國恩，為冑子師，代言禁林。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when the capital had fallen, Yi sighed: "I rose through Confucian learning, repeatedly receiving the state's grace, serving as tutor to the sons of officials and speaking for the forbidden gardens.
translations.idiomatic: In 1368, when the capital fell, Yi sighed, "Confucian study raised me; the dynasty heaped favor on me as tutor to its elite and voice of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 今縱無我戮，何面目見天下士乎！

translations.literal: Even if I were not executed, with what face could I meet the gentlemen of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Even if spared, how could I face the scholars of the empire?

sentences.zh: 」遂赴井而死，年六十一。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went and drowned himself in a well, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " He drowned himself in a well at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 有詩文傳於世。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose have been transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose survive.

sentences.zh: 柏帖穆爾，字君壽，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Baitiemuer, courtesy name Junshou, was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Baitiemuer, whose courtesy name was Junshou, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 家世歷履無所考。

translations.literal: His family's successive appointments cannot be traced.
translations.idiomatic: His family's official record is unknown.

sentences.zh: 居官所至，以廉能著聲。

translations.literal: Wherever he served in office, he was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held won renown for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 至正中，累遷為福建行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng period he was repeatedly promoted to be Director of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Fujian Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhizheng he rose to Director of the Left and Right Bureaus on the Fujian Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行省治福州。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat was administered from Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat was based at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大明以騎兵出杉關，取邵武，以舟師由海道趣閩，奄至城下。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Great Ming sent cavalry out through Shan Pass, took Shaowu, and sent a fleet by sea toward Min, suddenly arriving below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In 1367 Ming cavalry came through Shan Pass and seized Shaowu while a fleet advanced along the coast on Fujian, appearing suddenly beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 柏帖穆爾知城不可守，引妻妾坐樓上，慷慨謂曰：「丈夫死國，婦人死夫，義也。

translations.literal: Baitiemuer knew the city could not be held; he led his wife and concubines to sit upstairs and said generously: "A husband dies for his state, a wife dies for her husband—this is righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city could not be held, Baitiemuer brought his wife and concubines upstairs and said firmly, "A man dies for his country, a woman for her husband—that is righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今城且陷，吾必死於是，若等能吾從乎？

translations.literal: Now the city is about to fall; I must die here—can you follow me?
translations.idiomatic: The city will fall; I shall die here—will you follow me?"

sentences.zh: 」皆泣曰：「有死而已，無他志也。

translations.literal: " They all wept and said: "There is only death—no other wish.
translations.idiomatic: " They wept and said, "Death alone will do—we have no other wish.

sentences.zh: 」縊而死者六人。

translations.literal: " Six hanged themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Six died by hanging.

sentences.zh: 有十歲女，度其不能自死，則紿之曰：「汝稽顙拜佛，庶保我無恙也。

translations.literal: He had a ten-year-old daughter; judging that she could not kill herself, he deceived her, saying: "You kowtow and worship the Buddha—perhaps that will keep me unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: He had a ten-year-old daughter; knowing she could not take her own life, he tricked her: "Kowtow to the Buddha—it may keep me safe.

sentences.zh: 」甫拜，即挈米囊壓之死。

translations.literal: " As soon as she bowed, he immediately took a rice sack and pressed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The moment she bowed, he crushed her beneath a rice sack.

sentences.zh: 乳媼抱其幼子，旁立以泣，柏帖穆爾熟視之，歎曰：「父死國，母死夫，妾與女，從父者也，皆當死。

translations.literal: A wet nurse held his infant son, standing aside weeping; Baitiemuer looked at them long and sighed: "The father dies for the state, the mother dies for her husband, concubines and daughters follow the father—all ought to die.
translations.idiomatic: A nurse held his infant son, weeping nearby; Baitiemuer gazed at them and sighed, "A father dies for his country, a mother for her husband; concubines and daughters follow the father—all should die.

sentences.zh: 汝三歲兒，於義何所從乎？

translations.literal: Your three-year-old son—by righteousness, whom should he follow?
translations.idiomatic: Your three-year-old—what does duty require of him?

sentences.zh: 為宗祀計可也。

translations.literal: For the sake of the ancestral sacrifices, he may remain.
translations.idiomatic: For the lineage he may live.

sentences.zh: 」乃命媼抱匿旁近民舍，而斂金珠畀之曰：「即有緩急，可以此贖兒命。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the nurse to hold the child and hide in a nearby commoner's house, gathered gold and pearls and gave them to her, saying: "If there is any urgency, you may use these to ransom the boy's life.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the nurse hide the boy in a neighbor's house, gave her gold and pearls, and said, "If trouble comes, use these to buy his life.

sentences.zh: 」有頃，兵入城，即舉燈自燃，四圍窗火大發，遂自焚死。

translations.literal: " Before long the army entered the city; he immediately raised a lamp and set himself afire; flames burst from the windows all around, and he burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon soldiers entered; he lit a lamp and set himself ablaze; fire roared from every window and he perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 迭裡彌實，字子初，回回人。

translations.literal: Dielimishi, courtesy name Zichu, was a Hui Muslim.
translations.idiomatic: Dielimishi, whose courtesy name was Zichu, was a Hui Muslim.

sentences.zh: 性剛介，事母至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upright, and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and upright by nature, he was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 年四十，猶不仕，或問之，曰：「吾不忍舍吾母以去也。

translations.literal: At forty he still would not take office; when asked why, he said: "I cannot bear to leave my mother.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he still refused office; asked why, he said, "I cannot abandon my mother.

sentences.zh: 」以宿衛年勞，授行宣政院崇教，三遷為漳州路達魯花赤，居三年，居甚安之。

translations.literal: " For years of service in the palace guard he was appointed Chongjiao of the Xuanzheng Court on tour, and after three transfers became Darughachi of Zhangzhou Circuit; he lived there three years in great contentment.
translations.idiomatic: " Long palace-guard service won him Xuanzheng Court Chongjiao; three promotions later he was Darughachi of Zhangzhou, where he lived three peaceful years.

sentences.zh: 時陳有定據全閩，八郡之政，皆用其私人以總制之。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Youding held all Min; the government of the eight prefectures was entirely run by his private men as overall controllers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youding then held all Fujian; his men controlled every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命官，不得有所與。

translations.literal: Officials appointed by the court could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Court appointees could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 大明兵既取福州，興化、泉州皆納款。

translations.literal: After the Great Ming army had taken Fuzhou, Xinghua and Quanzhou both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ming forces took Fuzhou, Xinghua and Quanzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 或以告，迭裡彌實仰天歎曰：「吾不材，位三品，國恩厚矣，其何以報乎！

translations.literal: When someone reported this, Dielimishi looked up to heaven and sighed: "I am without talent, yet hold third rank—the state's grace is deep; how can I repay it!
translations.idiomatic: Told of this, Dielimishi looked heavenward and sighed, "I am unworthy of third rank, yet the dynasty favored me deeply—how repay it?

sentences.zh: 報國恩者，有死而已。

translations.literal: To repay the state's grace, there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: Only death repays such grace.

sentences.zh: 」亡何，吏走白招諭使者至，請出城迓之，迭裡彌實從容語之曰：「爾第往，吾行出矣。

translations.literal: " Before long an official ran in reporting that the pacification envoy had arrived and asked him to go out of the city to welcome him; Dielimishi said calmly: "You go on—I am about to go out.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon a clerk announced the pacification envoy and urged him to greet them outside the walls; Dielimishi said calmly, "You go—I am coming out now.

sentences.zh: 」乃詣廳事，具公服，北面再拜畢，引斧斫其印文，又大書手版曰「大元臣子」。

translations.literal: " He then went to the hall of government, put on full official dress, and after bowing twice facing north took an axe and chopped his seal inscription, and wrote large characters on his hand tablet: "Subject of the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He entered the hall in full dress, bowed twice north, chopped his seal with an axe, and wrote on his tablet: "Subject of the Great Yuan."

sentences.zh: 即入位端坐，拔所佩刀，剚喉中以死。

translations.literal: He then took his seat upright, drew the knife at his belt, and stabbed himself in the throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: He sat upright, drew his belt knife, and stabbed his throat.

sentences.zh: 既死，猶手執刀按膝坐，儼然如生時。

translations.literal: After death he still held the knife pressed to his knee as he sat, looking exactly as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Dead, he still gripped the knife on his knee, looking alive.

sentences.zh: 郡民相聚哭庭中，斂其屍，葬東門外。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture gathered to weep in the courtyard; they gathered his corpse and buried him outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: County folk wept in the courtyard, buried him outside the east gate.

sentences.zh: 時又有獲獨步丁者，回回人，舊進士，累官僉廣東廉訪司事；

translations.literal: At that time there was also Huo Dubuding, a Hui Muslim, a former jinshi, who had repeatedly served as Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Surveillance Commission;
translations.idiomatic: About then Huo Dubuding, a Hui Muslim and former jinshi, had been Vice Commissioner of Guangdong Surveillance;

sentences.zh: 有呂复者，為江西行省左右司都事。

translations.literal: there was Lu Fu, who was Director of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fu was Director of the Left and Right Bureaus on the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皆閒居，寓福州。

translations.literal: Both lived in retirement, residing at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Both lived in retirement at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 而復以行省命，攝長樂縣尹。

translations.literal: Fu, by order of the Branch Secretariat, acted as magistrate of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was acting magistrate of Changle on secretariat orders.

sentences.zh: 福州既下，獲獨步丁曰：「吾兄弟三人，皆忝進士，受國恩四十年，今雖無官守，然大節所在，其可辱乎！

translations.literal: After Fuzhou fell, Huo Dubuding said: "We three brothers are all jinshi in name, have received the state's grace for forty years; though we now hold no office, great principle is at stake—how could we endure disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhou fell, Huo Dubuding said, "We three brothers are jinshi who have eaten the state's grain forty years; though without office now, how bear such shame?

sentences.zh: 」以石自係其腰，投井死。

translations.literal: " He tied a stone to his waist and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: " He weighted his waist with stone and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 复亦曰：「吾世食君祿，今雖攝官，若不以死報國，則無以見先人於地下。

translations.literal: Fu also said: "Our family has eaten the ruler's salary for generations; though I now hold office only in an acting capacity, if I do not die to repay the state, I cannot face my ancestors underground.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "My line has fed on royal salary for generations; though only acting magistrate, without dying for the state I cannot face my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」引繩自經死。

translations.literal: " He took a rope and hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 獲獨步丁兄曰穆魯丁者，官建康；

translations.literal: Huo Dubuding's elder brother, called Muruding, held office at Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Dubuding's elder brother Muruding served at Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 曰海魯丁者，官信州。

translations.literal: the one called Hailuding held office at Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hailuding served at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，亦皆死國難云。

translations.literal: Earlier, they too had all died in the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: They too had earlier died for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 樸賽因不花，字德中，肅良合台人。

translations.literal: Pusaiyinbuhua, courtesy name Dezhong, was a man of the Sulianghetai people.
translations.idiomatic: Pusaiyinbuhua, whose courtesy name was Dezhong, was a Sulianghetai tribesman.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善騎射。

translations.literal: He had great physical strength and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 由速古兒赤授利器庫提點，再轉為資正院判官，累遷同知樞密院事，遷翰林學士，尋升承旨，賜虎符，兼巡軍合浦全羅等處軍民萬戶都元帥，除大司農，出為嶺北行省右丞，昇平章政事。

translations.literal: From Sugur-chi he was appointed Director of the Arsenal Depot, then transferred to be Vice Director of the Zizheng Court, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Privy Council, moved to Hanlin Academician, soon elevated to Academician Expositor, granted a tiger tally, concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the military households of Hepu, Jeolla, and other places, appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture, sent out as Right Councilor of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat, and promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: From palace guard he became Arsenal Director, then Zizheng Court Vice Director, Privy Council Vice Director, Hanlin Academician, then Expositor with a tiger tally, concurrently commander in Hepu and Jeolla, Grand Minister of Agriculture, Lingbei Right Councilor, and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 至正二十四年，甘肅行省以孛羅帖木兒矯弒皇后、皇孫，遣人白事，平章政事也速答兒即欲署諭眾榜，樸賽因不花持不可曰： 「此大事，何得輕​​信，況非符驗公文。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhizheng, the Gansu Branch Secretariat reported that Boluotiemuer had falsely murdered the empress and the imperial grandson and sent men to inform the court; Grand Councilor Yesudaer immediately wished to issue a proclamation to the masses; Pusaiyinbuhua held that it should not be done, saying: "This is a great matter—how can it be lightly believed, especially when it is not an authenticated official document.
translations.idiomatic: In 1364 Gansu reported Boluotiemuer had murdered empress and imperial grandson; Grand Councilor Yesudaer wanted a public notice; Pusaiyinbuhua refused: "This is grave—how believe it without authenticated documents?

sentences.zh: 」卒不署榜。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not sign the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: " He never signed the notice.

sentences.zh: 既而果妄傳。

translations.literal: Afterward it proved to be a false rumor.
translations.idiomatic: It proved a false rumor.

sentences.zh: 會皇太子撫軍冀寧，承製拜樸賽因不花翰林學士承旨，遷集賢大學士，又為宣政院使，遂拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was pacifying the army at Jining, by imperial commission Pusaiyinbuhua was appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor, moved to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, again made Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court, and then appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince campaigned at Jining, he was made Hanlin Expositor, Grand Academician, Xuanzheng Commissioner, then Central Secretariat Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 大明兵逼京師，詔樸賽因不花以兵守順承門，其所領兵僅數百羸卒而已。

translations.literal: When the Great Ming army pressed the capital, an edict ordered Pusaiyinbuhua to hold Shuncheng Gate with troops; the soldiers he led were only several hundred weak and worn men.
translations.idiomatic: As Ming troops closed on the capital, he was ordered to hold Shuncheng Gate with a few hundred exhausted men.

sentences.zh: 乃嘆息謂左右曰：「國事至此，吾但知與此門同存亡也。

translations.literal: He sighed to those beside him: "The state has come to this—I know only to live or die with this gate.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed to his attendants, "The realm has come to this—I live or die with this gate.

sentences.zh: 」城陷被執，以見主將，唯請速死，不少屈。

translations.literal: " When the city fell he was seized and brought before the commander; he only asked to die quickly and would not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: " Captured when the city fell, he asked only for a swift death and would not bend.

sentences.zh: 主將命留營中，終不屈，殺之。

translations.literal: The commander ordered him kept in camp; in the end he would not submit and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander kept him in camp; he never yielded and was killed.

sentences.zh: 是時有張庸者，字存中，溫州人。

translations.literal: At that time there was Zhang Yong, courtesy name Cunzhong, a man of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: About then Zhang Yong of Wenzhou, courtesy name Cunzhong,

sentences.zh: 性豪爽，精太乙數，會世亂，以策幹經略使李國鳳，承製授庸福建行省員外郎，治兵杉關。

translations.literal: Bold and generous by nature, skilled in Taiyi numerology; when the age was in turmoil he presented stratagems to the pacification commissioner Li Guofeng and was appointed by commission Assistant Department Director of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, drilling troops at Shan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: was bold, versed in Taiyi numerology, and in the turmoil offered plans to Li Guofeng, winning appointment as Fujian Branch Assistant Director to drill troops at Shan Pass.

sentences.zh: 頃之，計事赴京師，因進《太乙數圖》，順帝喜之，擢秘書少監。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he went to the capital on business and presented Chart of Taiyi Numerology; Emperor Shundi was pleased and promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went to the capital with business and presented his Taiyi chart; the emperor made him Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 皇太子立大撫軍院，命庸團結房山，遷同僉將作院事，又除刑部尚書，仍領團結。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince established the Great Pacification Army Bureau, Yong was ordered to organize militia in Fangshan, moved to be Associate Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, again appointed Minister of Punishments while still leading the militia organization.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince formed the Great Pacification Army Bureau, Yong organized Fangshan militia, became Associate Palace Buildings Director, then Minister of Punishments while still leading militia.

sentences.zh: 會諸寨既降，庸守駱駝谷，遣從事段禎請援於擴廓帖木兒，不報。

translations.literal: When the various stockades had surrendered, Yong held Luotuo Valley, sent his staff member Duan Zhen to request aid from Kökö Temür, and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When other strongholds surrendered, Yong held Luotuo Valley and sent Duan Zhen to Kökö Temür for aid without reply.

sentences.zh: 庸獨堅守拒戰，眾將潰，庸無去志。

translations.literal: Yong alone held firm and fought off attacks; the generals broke and fled, but Yong had no thought of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Yong alone held out; his officers fled but he would not leave.

sentences.zh: 已而寨民李世傑執庸出降，以見主將，庸不屈，與禎同被殺。

translations.literal: Before long the stockade people Li Shijie seized Yong and brought him out to surrender; when brought before the commander, Yong would not submit and was killed together with Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Shijie of the stockade seized him and surrendered him; before the commander he would not yield and was killed with Zhen.

sentences.zh: 丁好禮，字敬可，真定蠡州人。

translations.literal: Ding Haoli, courtesy name Jingke, was a man of Li County in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Haoli, courtesy name Jingke, came from Li County in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 精律算，初試吏於戶部，辟中書掾，授戶部主事，擢江南行台監察御史，復入戶部為員外郎，拜監察御史，又入戶部為郎中，升侍郎。

translations.literal: Skilled in law and calculation, he first tried service as a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was recruited as a Central Secretariat staff member, appointed Revenue Main Clerk, promoted to Investigating Censor on the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, returned to Revenue as Assistant Department Director, appointed Investigating Censor, again entered Revenue as Director, and promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in law and reckoning, he began in Revenue, became Secretariat staff, Revenue Main Clerk, Jiangnan Investigating Censor, Revenue Assistant Director, Investigating Censor again, Revenue Director, then Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 除京畿漕運使，建議置司於通州，重講究漕運利病，著為成法，人皆便之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region, proposed establishing an office at Tongzhou, thoroughly investigated the pros and cons of canal transport, set them down as established regulations, and everyone found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Named Capital Region Transport Commissioner, he proposed a Tongzhou office, studied canal transport thoroughly, and set lasting rules everyone welcomed.

sentences.zh: 除戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時國家多故，財用空乏，好禮能撙節浮費，國家用度，賴之以給。

translations.literal: At that time the state had many troubles and finances were empty; Haoli could curtail wasteful spending, and the state's expenditures relied on him to be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil and coffers bare; Haoli cut waste and kept the treasury supplied.

sentences.zh: 拜參議中書省事，遷治書侍御史，出為遼陽行省左丞，未行，留為樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Councilor of the Central Secretariat, moved to Investigating Censor, sent out as Left Councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat; before he set out he was retained as Vice Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was Secretariat Councilor, Investigating Censor, then Liaoyang Left Councilor; before leaving he was kept as Privy Council Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，遂拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng he was then appointed Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1360 he became Central Secretariat Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時京師大饑，天壽節，廟堂欲用故事大宴會，好禮言：「今民父子有相食者，君臣當修省，以弭大患，燕會宜減常度。

translations.literal: At that time the capital suffered great famine; on the Emperor's Birthday the court wished to hold the customary grand banquet; Haoli said: "Now fathers and sons among the people are eating one another—the ruler and ministers ought to cultivate themselves to quell great calamity; feasts should be reduced below the usual scale.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the capital; on the emperor's birthday the court wanted the usual feast; Haoli said, "Families are eating one another—ruler and ministers should repent, not feast as usual.

sentences.zh: 」不聽，乞謝事，乃以集賢大學士致仕，給全俸家居。

translations.literal: " They did not listen; he requested to resign and was allowed to retire as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies with full salary at home.
translations.idiomatic: " Ignored, he asked to retire as Grand Academician with full pay at home.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒扈從皇太子還京，輸山東粟以遺朝貴，饋好禮麥百石，好禮不受。

translations.literal: When Kökö Temür escorted the Crown Prince back to the capital, he sent Shandong grain as gifts to court nobles and presented Haoli with a hundred piculs of wheat; Haoli would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Kökö Temür, escorting the Crown Prince home, sent Shandong grain to court nobles and offered Haoli a hundred piculs of wheat; he refused.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復起為中書平章政事，尋以論議不合，謝政去，特封趙國公。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was again raised to be Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat; soon, because discussions did not agree, he resigned from government and was specially enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1367 he was again Grand Councilor; soon he resigned over policy disputes and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 大明兵入京城，或勉其謁大將，好禮叱之曰：「我以小吏致位極品，爵上公，今老矣，恨無以報國，所欠惟一死耳。

translations.literal: When the Great Ming army entered the capital, some urged him to call on the commander; Haoli rebuked them: "I rose from a petty clerk to the highest rank, ennobled as a grand duke; now I am old, and regret only that I cannot repay the state—the one thing left is a single death.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming troops entered the capital, some urged him to visit the commander; Haoli snapped, "I rose from a clerk to the highest rank and a grand duke; I am old and owe the state only one death.

sentences.zh: 」後數日，大將召好禮，不肯行，舁至齊化門，抗辭不屈而死，年七十五。

translations.literal: " Several days later the commander summoned Haoli; he would not go and was carried to Qihua Gate, where he spoke defiantly and died unyielding, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: " Days later the commander summoned him; he refused, was carried to Qihua Gate, defied them, and died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 是日，中書參知政事郭庸亦舁至齊化門，眾叱之拜，庸曰：「臣各為其主，死自吾分，何拜之有！

translations.literal: That same day Vice Councilor Guo Yong was also carried to Qihua Gate; the crowd shouted at him to bow; Yong said: "Each minister serves his own lord—death is my portion; what bowing is there!
translations.idiomatic: That day Vice Councilor Guo Yong was also brought to Qihua Gate; the crowd ordered him to bow; Yong said, "Each serves his sovereign—death is mine; why bow?

sentences.zh: 」語不少屈而死。

translations.literal: " He spoke without yielding in the least and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not yield and died.

sentences.zh: 庸字允中，蒙古氏，由國學生釋褐出身，累遷為陝西行台監察御史，與同列劾知樞密院事也先帖木兒喪師，左遷中興總管府判官。

translations.literal: Yong, courtesy name Yunzhong, was of the Mongol clan; from a student of the Imperial Academy he entered service, was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and together with colleagues impeached the Privy Council Director Yesentiemuer for losing the army, being demoted to Vice Magistrate of the Zhongxing Circuit General Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, courtesy name Yunzhong, was Mongol, entered from the Imperial Academy, became Shaanxi Investigating Censor, and with colleagues impeached Privy Council Director Yesentiemuer for losing armies, demoted to Zhongxing Vice Magistrate.

sentences.zh: 其後也先帖木兒以罪黜，召拜監察御史，累轉參政中書，其節義與好禮並云。

translations.literal: Afterward Yesentiemuer was dismissed for crime and recalled as Investigating Censor; after repeated transfers he became Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat; his integrity and righteousness are ranked together with Haoli's.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yesentiemuer was dismissed and Yong was recalled as Investigating Censor, rising to Secretariat Vice Councilor; his loyalty matches Haoli's.
